solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shrewd language little good in front of heartless heavyweight journalist

parts.note: Farsi is the Persian language of Iran
G is a short form of good

indicators.note: heartless strips away everything between the first and last letters of the word heavyweight

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A shrewd hack is described as a hefty writer who speaks a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves HT from heavyweight; 'in front of' simply orders the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone far-sighted plans wisely for the future, so the word means astute or shrewd.

clue.text: Pay no attention to Italian gentleman with face cut

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so cutting it drops the opening letter of the Italian title

parts.note: signore is the Italian title for a man, like Mr or sir

explanation.surface: Someone snubs an Italian man who has a scarred face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with face cut' removes the S at the front of SIGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to disregard it, deliberately paying it no heed.

clue.text: Modified crop study shortly will deliver results

indicators.note: modified signals that the letters of crop and the shortened study are changed into a new order
shortly means the word study is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the clue word itself, trimmed before being mixed in

explanation.surface: A study of genetically modified crops promises to yield findings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims study to STUD; 'Modified' then reworks CROP and STUD together.
explanation.definitionFit: A product is an outcome, the result of a process or calculation.

clue.text: Rarely is student wearing revolutionary fashions

indicators.note: wearing means the learner letter is clothed by the turned word around it
revolutionary means turning over, so the word for fashions is read backwards

parts.note: modes are fashions or styles
L is a learner, as on a British L-plate

explanation.surface: A student hardly ever dresses in radical clothing styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns MODES into SEDOM; 'wearing' puts the L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means not often, the same as infrequently or rarely.

clue.text: Quarrel said to erupt with sarcastic expression describing Republican

indicators.note: erupting throws things out violently, so the letters of said burst into a new order
describing is used in its sense of drawing round, so the exclamation encloses the party letter

parts.note: gee, as in 'gee, thanks', is said with heavy irony

explanation.surface: An argument flares up when someone mocks a Republican with a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around; 'to erupt' is the anagram signal for said.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree is to hold opposite views, and so to argue or fall out.

clue.text: Sufficient number barely realising what follows what comes next?

indicators.note: barely is read as bare, stripped of its covering, so the outside letters of the word for enough fall away

parts.note: plenty means enough of something, a sufficient amount

explanation.surface: A puzzled musing on whether there is barely enough to understand what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the next clue down, 7 Down, Shrove Tuesday: the season it refers to begins the day after.
explanation.definitionFit: The forty days of fasting before Easter start on Ash Wednesday, straight after Pancake Day.

clue.text: Boast made by German after chat about restricting weight

indicators.note: after puts the German abbreviation behind the rest
restricting means hemming in, so the turned word for chat closes around the weight letter
about means turned round, so the word for chat is read backwards

parts.note: gas is idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: A German brags after a conversation about keeping his weight down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns GAS into SAG; 'restricting' puts W inside it, giving SWAG.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger is to strut and brag, showing off with a boastful air.

clue.text: You've hat and dress sorted for spring blow-out?

indicators.note: sorted signals that all these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Having got your hat and outfit ready for a big seasonal party.
explanation.walkthrough: A blow-out is a feast: the day before Lent was traditionally for using up rich food, hence pancakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancake Day falls in late winter or early spring and is a last feast before the fasting season.

clue.text: Distinguished artist given space alongside foremost of talents

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist
an en is a printer's space, half an em wide

indicators.note: foremost of picks the opening letter of the word talents

explanation.surface: A notable artist is given room alongside the most gifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin, a British artist famous for 'My Bed', is a favourite crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent person is famous and respected, distinguished in their field.

clue.text: Worried vet heartened by British missing equestrian competition

indicators.note: worried is read as agitated or disturbed, so the letters are shaken into a new order
missing means the British letter is taken away from the word by

explanation.surface: An anxious vet cheers up when a British entrant drops out of a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartened' looks like a container signal but is plain fodder; 'missing' leaves only Y of by for the pool that 'Worried' mixes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing tests a horse and rider over dressage, cross-country and show jumping, traditionally on separate days.

clue.text: Acknowledged grass is necessary around small garden feature

indicators.note: around means the word for grass goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
a pond is a common feature of a garden

explanation.surface: Someone confirmed that a small pond must be ringed by grasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal; 'is necessary' just links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have responded is to have replied, which is acknowledging a message.

clue.text: Bloomer, or catastrophe to pull out police officers?

indicators.note: pull out means withdraw, so the officers leave the word for catastrophe

parts.note: a disaster is a catastrophe
DIs are detective inspectors

explanation.surface: Is this a mistake, or a disaster that calls for the police to withdraw?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' tempts as a blunder, but here it is literal: something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are daisy-like garden flowers, so in crosswords one is a flowering plant, a bloomer.

clue.text: Unclear if magazine's accepting article to replace others originally

indicators.note: to replace means the article goes in where the letter from others stood

parts.note: Vogue is the fashion magazine

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of the word others

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: It is unclear whether a magazine will take a piece in place of earlier ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps the O of VOGUE (the first of 'others') for A; 'accepting' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague is imprecise or hazy, not clear in meaning or outline.

clue.text: City accountant, male needing some dental work

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a bridge is a dental fitting holding false teeth

explanation.surface: An accountant from town is a man needing treatment at the dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is an English university city in East Anglia.

clue.text: Something done to keep period at home fixed

indicators.note: to keep means the word for something done holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a deed is an act, something done
a term is a period of time
in means at home

explanation.surface: A household task kept a person indoors for a fixed spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' is the container signal; 'fixed' is the definition in its sense of settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined can mean settled or decided, as a fixed price is a determined one.

clue.text: Three times required to ring university? Extremely upset son expresses disapproval

indicators.note: to ring means the Ts surround the university letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so three of them make three Ts

indicators.note: extremely picks only the end letters of the word upset

explanation.surface: Someone tries three times to phone a university, and a very upset son voices his displeasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ring' (surround) and 'Extremely' (outer letters) are the signals; 'Three times' means three copies of the letter for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'tut' twice is the clicking sound people make to show they disapprove.

clue.text: Fearless peacekeepers advanced and became edgy, reportedly …

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for became edgy is given by its sound only

parts.note: frayed describes edges coming apart, and nerves worn thin

explanation.surface: Bold peacekeepers moved forward and then grew nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes FRAYED sound like FRAID. The ellipsis just links to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Unafraid means without fear, so brave or fearless.

clue.text: Airline occasionally kept charge back on board for hot drink

indicators.note: on board means placed inside, as within the airline's name

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: back means the letters taken from kept plus the charge are read in reverse
occasionally takes every other letter of the word kept

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: An airline sometimes kept a charge back for a hot drink served in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes ET from kept; with FEE that gives ETFEE, and 'back' turns it into EEFTE, which goes 'on board' BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a hot broth made by steeping beef, drunk as a warming beverage.

clue.text: … significant moment defending second display of force

indicators.note: defending means guarding, so the pieces close around the letter for second

parts.note: big means important or significant
a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A key moment protects someone's second, continuing the previous clue's bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' is the container signal. 'Just a tick' is British for 'just a moment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Big-stick policy means threatening military might, from Roosevelt's 'speak softly and carry a big stick'.

clue.text: Repeatedly discovered Wendy fears bingo is becoming attractive

indicators.note: discovered means having its cover removed, and repeatedly applies it to each word, so each loses its outside letters

explanation.surface: Wendy's fear of bingo becomes charming once found out again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncovering wENDy, fEARs and bINGo leaves END, EAR and ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Endearing means inspiring affection, so charming or attractive.

clue.text: Colour that's receding in sheepdog I'd nicknamed

indicators.note: receding says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dog owner explains a colour by the nickname given to a sheepdog.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named 'in' as nothing and put 'that's' in the definition; 'that's' only links, and 'in' signals the letters are tucked inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet hue, one of the seven in the rainbow.

clue.text: Sudden increase in material being broadcast

indicators.note: being broadcast means the word for the cloth is spoken over the air, so only its sound counts

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled cloth

explanation.surface: A spike in the amount of fabric being sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being broadcast' makes SERGE sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden rush or powerful upswing, as in a surge of demand.

clue.text: Give support to subordinate

definitions.meaning: to back a motion formally, as a seconder does

explanation.surface: Back up a junior colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A seconder backs a proposal; a second-rate thing ranks below the first.

clue.text: Person who gives name entering house, say

indicators.note: entering means the name letter goes into the word for house

parts.note: a door stands for a house, as in 'two doors down'

explanation.surface: A benefactor gives their name on coming into a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that DOOR stands for a house only loosely, as in 'next door'.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a benefactor who contributes money, blood or organs.

clue.text: All-points bulletin?

parts.note: an all-points bulletin is a police alert; here it means a report gathered from north, east, west and south

explanation.walkthrough: The compass points N, E, W, S give the letters, a bulletin covering every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast bulletin reports current events, and its four letters are the compass points.

clue.text: Policeman from Vice vetted criminal, one very withdrawn

indicators.note: criminal is read as wrong or crooked, so the letters of Vice and vetted are put into a corrupt new order
withdrawn means the single very letter is taken out of the pooled letters before they are rearranged

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very, and there is only one to take out

explanation.surface: A detective from the Vice squad, vetted as a crook, has gone very quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: VICE and VETTED hold two Vs; 'withdrawn' removes one, and 'criminal' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective is a plain-clothes police officer who investigates crimes.

clue.text: Drowsy and moving unsteadily, about close to exhaustion

indicators.note: about means the word for moving unsteadily goes round that letter

parts.note: yawing is swinging off course, as a ship or aircraft does

indicators.note: close to picks the closing letter of the word exhaustion

explanation.surface: Someone sleepy and swaying, nearly worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside YAWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Yawning is what a sleepy person does, so it describes being drowsy.

clue.text: Capacity to provide satisfaction

explanation.surface: Having the ability to please.
explanation.walkthrough: Stress shifts between the two senses: CONtent for the amount held, conTENT for happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The volume held is its contents; being content is feeling satisfied.
